Next, let's read in our data. 

```{r read.data}
counts = read.csv('data/abx_cohort_rarefied_counts.csv',
                  colClasses = c(X = "character"))

names(counts)[1] <- "public_client_id"

rownames(counts) <- counts$public_client_id
counts$public_client_id <- NULL
counts_matrix <- as.matrix(counts)
```

```{r enterotypes}
fit <- readRDS("data/abx_users_dmm_fit.rds")
bic  <- sapply(fit, BIC)
plot(bic, type="b", xlab="Number of Dirichlet Components", ylab="Model Fit")
```


```{r choose.min}
best <- which.min(bic)  # or pick manually, e.g. best <- 4
best_fit <- fit[[best]]
```

# assign clusters for our script run

```{r}
# Sample-level cluster assignments
clusters <- apply(mixture(best_fit), 1, which.max)
result_df <- data.frame(sample = rownames(counts), cluster = clusters) # clusters
#result_df$mixture_probs <- mixture(best_fit)                           # probs
write.csv(result_df,
          "data/dmm_clusters_mixture_probs_arivale_abx_recency_cohort.csv")
```

Look at feature weights.

```{r}
# Feature (taxon) weights per cluster
feature_weights <- as.data.frame(fitted(best_fit))
colnames(feature_weights) <- c("c1", "c2", "c3", "c4")
#write.csv(feature_weights, "data/dmm_feature_weights_arivale_abx.csv")
```

```{r heatmap.feat.weights}
feature_matrix <- as.matrix(feature_weights)
heatmap(feature_matrix)
```
Let's subset to find the most important features

```{r}
df_long <- feature_weights |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("feature") |>
  pivot_longer(
    -feature,
    names_to = "cluster",
    values_to = "weight"
  )

df_long |>
  group_by(cluster) |>
  slice_max(weight, n = 15) |>
   dplyr::arrange(cluster, desc(weight))
```

```{r}
top_df_long <- df_long |>
  group_by(cluster) |>
  slice_max(weight, n = 15) |>
  ungroup()

top_features <- unique(top_df_long$feature) # select features
top_df <- feature_weights[top_features, ]   # select columns from large df
mat <- as.matrix(top_df)                    # make into matrix
rownames(mat) <- str_wrap(rownames(top_df), # wrap names
                          width = 30)

Heatmap(
  mat,
  row_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 6),
  row_names_side = "left",
)
```

Okay now calculate specificity

```{r specificity.for.enterotypes}
specificity <- apply(feature_weights, 1, function(x) {
  max(x) - mean(x[-which.max(x)]) # calcs the difference between max and avg of other 3
})

feature_cluster <- apply(feature_weights, 1, which.max) # finds which cluster most associated

spec_df <- data.frame(
  feature = rownames(feature_weights),
  assigned_cluster = feature_cluster,  # which cluster a feature is most associated with
  specificity = specificity            # diff between that and the other clusters
)

# This would show the top features for cluster 1
spec_df |>
  dplyr::filter(assigned_cluster == 1) |>
  dplyr::arrange(desc(specificity))

# Select top 10 features for each cluster
top_distinguishing <- spec_df |>
  group_by(assigned_cluster) |>
  slice_max(specificity, n = 10)

# Find all features that were in this top 10
features <- top_distinguishing$feature

mat <- as.matrix(feature_weights[features, ])
rownames(mat) <- stringr::str_wrap(rownames(mat), 30)

# row-wise z-score scaling
mat_scaled <- t(scale(t(mat)))

Heatmap(
  mat_scaled,
  name = "Z-score",
  cluster_columns = FALSE,
  row_names_side = "left",
  row_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 6),
  row_names_max_width = grid::unit(12, "cm")
)
```


```{r plot.specificity}
# entero_map = {1:'Rum',2:'Bac1',3:'Bac2',4:'Prev'}
pheatmap(
  mat,  # should be same data as blue heatmap two above, but scale and cluster rows
  scale = "row",
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  fontsize_row = 5
)
```

## Okay well let's continue with our own analysis for now!

```{r assign.entero.labels}
result_df <- result_df %>%
  mutate(
    enterotype = case_when(
      cluster == 1 ~ "Bac1",
      cluster == 2 ~ "Rum",
      cluster == 3 ~ "Bac2",
      cluster == 4 ~ "Prev"
    )
  )
```

# Awesome, move onto clinical chems and metadata

```{r create.med.context}
# This will paste the text along with the variable condition
# None will be -
# Users will be +
abx_entero_labs_micro$med_context <- paste0(
  "abx ", ifelse(abx_entero_labs_micro$abx_recency == "none", "-", "+"), " / ",
  "statin ", ifelse(abx_entero_labs_micro$statin_binary == "Yes", "+", "-")
)

# Create a new df to look at instances for each med context
plot_data <- dplyr::count(
  abx_entero_labs_micro,      # In this df
  med_context,                # Within each group
  enterotype,                 # Count the enterotypes
  name = "enterotype_count")

# Next we should count the med contexts to calculate proportions
med_context_count <- dplyr::count(
  abx_entero_labs_micro,            # In df
  med_context,                      # count med_context
  name = "med_context_count")

# Now left join on plot data to propagate the med_context sums
plot_data <- dplyr::left_join(
  plot_data,                      
  med_context_count,
  by = "med_context"
)

# Now let's calculate the percentage of each enterotype within context
plot_data <- group_by(plot_data, med_context)
plot_data <- mutate(
  plot_data,                          # In this df
  total_N = enterotype_count,         # New col for total N
  percentage = (enterotype_count      # Calculate percentable
                / med_context_count),
  x_label_with_N = paste0(            # Make x-axis label
    med_context, "\n(N = ",
    enterotype_count, ")")
)

plot_data <- ungroup(plot_data)
```

```{r enterotype.enrichment.plot}
color_scheme=c(
  "Prev"="yellowgreen",
  "Rum"="orange",
  "Bac1"="#088888",
  "Bac2"="#A280AE"
)

ggplot(abx_entero_labs_micro, aes(x = med_context, fill = enterotype)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_scheme) + 
  geom_text(stat = "count",
            aes(label = scales::percent(
              after_stat(count / tapply(count, x, sum)[x]),
              accuracy = 1
              )),
    position = position_fill(vjust = 0.5)
  ) +

  # Simplest way to add (N=) to X-axis: calculate counts dynamically right here
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "\n(N = ", table(abx_entero_labs_micro$med_context)[x], ")")
  ) +
  theme(text=element_text(size=14)) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")) +
  labs(y = "Enterotype Distribution (%)", x = "Medication Use")
```

The above is for the med contexts with statin. What about antibiotic recency?

# Look at enrichment of Bac2 versus other enterotypes

```{r bac2.abx.recency}
abx_entero_labs_micro$bac2 <- ifelse(abx_entero_labs_micro$enterotype == "Bac2",
                                     1,  # Bac2
                                     0)  # All other enterotypes

abx_entero_labs_micro$bac2 <- factor(abx_entero_labs_micro$bac2)

bac2_logit_abx_recency <- glm(bac2 ~ age + sex + centered_BMI + vendor_dashboard + 
                    PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + centered_eGFR +
                    abx_recency + statin_binary,
                    family = binomial(), data = abx_entero_labs_micro)

summary(bac2_logit_abx_recency)
```


```{r bac2.abx.year}
abx_entero_labs_micro$bac2 <- ifelse(abx_entero_labs_micro$enterotype == "Bac2",
                                     1,  # Bac2
                                     0)  # All other enterotypes

abx_entero_labs_micro$bac2 <- factor(abx_entero_labs_micro$bac2)

bac2_logit <- glm(bac2 ~ age + sex + centered_BMI + vendor_dashboard + 
                    PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + centered_eGFR +
                    abx_year*statin_binary,
    family = binomial(), data = abx_entero_labs_micro)

summary(bac2_logit)
```
